facts.text: In 1521, King Christian II invited Dutch farmers to Amager to grow vegetables for Copenhagen, earning the island the nickname "pantry of Copenhagen".
Amager’s northern part belongs to Copenhagen Municipality, while its southern tip forms Dragør Municipality, a historic fishing village.
The island connects to Zealand by eight bridges and a metro tunnel, and to Sweden via the Øresund Bridge.
Amager Strandpark, neglected since the 1930s, was fully redeveloped between 2004 and 2005 into a popular coastal park.
During WWII, authorities drained part of the sea west of Amager and built a dam, adding 20 km² to the island in 1943.
The Dutch settlers on Amager kept their own language, Amager Dutch, which survived until 1858 despite a ban on mixed marriages.
